title: Mortality rate attributed to cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes or chronic respiratory disease
graph_title: Mortality rate attributed to cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes or chronic respiratory disease
national_indicator_available: Mortality rate attributed to cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes or chronic respiratory disease
national_indicator_description: The World Health Organization (WHO) tracks noncommunicable diseases mortality as the mortality rate attributed to cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes or chronic respiratory disease.
computation_definitions: Premature mortality due to noncommunicable diseases is defined as the propability of dying between age 30 and exact age 70 from any of cardiovascular diseases, cancer, diabetes, or chronic respiratory diseases.
computation_calculations: This indicator is calculated using life table methods; see the global metadata link for more details.
other_info: Additional data on noncommunicable diseases in Rwanda may be found in the [Non-Communicable Diseases Annual Reports](https://www.moh.gov.rw/health-reports) published by the Ministry of Health (MoH).
comments_limitations: For more details on methodology, see the linked data source.
indicator_definition: Mortality rate attributed to cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes or chronic respiratory disease is defined as the probability of dying between the ages of 30 and 70 years from cardiovascular diseases, cancer, diabetes or chronic respiratory diseases, defined as the percent of 30-year-old-people who would die before their 70th birthday from cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes, or chronic respiratory disease, assuming that they would experience current mortality rates at every age and they would not die from any other cause of death (e.g., injuries or HIV/AIDS).
